title: Type-Changing Schema Evolution (Truncation and Precision Loss)
pattern: Altering a primitive field's numeric width or type signature in a binary schema while keeping the same tag ID.
why_bad: If a newer v2 application writes a 64-bit value that exceeds the bounds of a 32-bit integer (e.g., `4,294,967,296`), and an older v1 application reads it using the 32-bit schema, the value will be truncated or corrupted on deserialization [632].
detection: Type signatures of the same tag ID changing between schema revisions where the target type represents a wider byte representation than the source type.
counterexample: None. Changing primitive bit widths on existing tags violates safe schema evolution guarantees.
source: Designing Data-Intensive Applications, Chapter 4, "Protobuf / Thrift / Avro compatibility" [632]
